VitaNutra Foods Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaNutra Foods Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then 1 on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaNutra Foods Inc.'s Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Growth Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on five key areas: impact of new product innovations and launches, discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, capital expenditure plans and priorities, organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year, and revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance.

First, regarding impact of new product innovations and launches: Our recent NPD efforts have been a standout, generating hundreds of millions in revenue and accelerating growth in high-margin categories like functional beverages and plant-based snacks.

Second, concerning discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: We've executed disciplined pricing to counter input cost pressures while maintaining volume stability through premium mix shifts.

Third, in terms of capital expenditure plans and priorities: Our capex investments are targeted at capacity, automation, sustainability, and maintenance to support long-term resilience and returns.

Fourth, looking at organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter/year: We're guiding to solid growth in Q4 and FY2025, driven by volume recovery and pricing optimization across regions and segments.

Finally, reviewing revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance: We're reaffirming our outlook with confidence, reflecting strength in core trends and operational execution.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $2.85 billion, representing an 8.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.5%, impacted by elevated input costs in commodities like cocoa and dairy but offset by productivity gains and pricing actions. Operating income was $650 million, and earnings per share were $0.95. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $2.0 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Building on the key areas Alex highlighted, let me provide deeper insights, starting with the impact of our new product innovations and launches. In the Food & Beverage industry, where categories face maturity and private label pressures, innovation is essential for premiumization and share gains against leaders like PepsiCo or Monster.

In Q3, our NPD portfolio—products launched in the last 24 months—generated $285 million in net revenue, or 18% of total segment sales, with 22% year-over-year growth. This surpassed our overall 11% top-line increase and boosted gross margins by 320 basis points to 42.5% on these items, thanks to 15-20% premium pricing and efficient formulations.

Our approach rests on health & wellness, sustainability, and indulgence. We've upped R&D to $145 million this year, a 12% rise, emphasizing clean labels, fermentation for sweeteners, and upcycled ingredients to handle 25-30% inflation in sugar and cocoa from Brazil and West Africa disruptions.

Key launches include ZestRevive functional beverages, rolled out Q1 in North America: RTD with adaptogens, nootropics, zero sugar, 50 calories—echoing Celsius growth. It reached $120 million in trailing sales, 85% ACV in grocery and convenience, 48% gross margins via e-com (15% volume) and lower cold-chain needs. North America drove 70%, with UK Tesco traction at 25% monthly repeats.

VitaCrunch plant-based snacks, Q2 global: pea protein, upcycled veggies, 12g protein/100 calories for the $10B+ market at 28% CAGR. $95 million YTD, 5 points to snack growth, 1.2 share points gained. Micro-encapsulation cuts sodium 15%, appealing to millennials. APAC China up 45% QoQ on Tmall/JD.

EcoBloom premium mixers, Q3: botanical low-ABV for non-alc trend like Athletic Brewing. $70 million run-rate, 30% bar/spirits channel boost, 22% US household penetration via Whole Foods/Total Wine. 100% recyclable Tetra Pak with 30% PCR lifted loyalty 35%.

Regionally: North America 55% of NPD at 28% YoY on omnichannel wellness; EMEA 25% at 15% with EU Green Deal; APAC/LATAM 20% at 35% from urban Brazil/Indonesia ($25M incremental).

These tie into SKU rationalization (12% pruned), 12 co-man deals cutting capex 20%, and pipeline with AI flavors, regenerative ag for cocoa at $4,200/ton. NPD should drive 20-25% of 2025 growth, 200-300 bps EBITDA lift at 90% ACV.

Next, on pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: This quarter's resilient top-line, with net revenues up 8.2% to $2.85 billion and fifth straight quarter above 7% organic, stems from our RGM framework balancing pricing, volume, and mix in Snacks, Beverages, and Dairy.

We implemented 6.1% average price hikes globally, up from 5.4% in Q2, responding to 12-15% COGS inflation: cocoa +22% (West Africa, like Mondelez/Hershey), dairy proteins +14% (EU supply), oils +18% (palm/sunflower). Granular via elasticity models.

Snacks (42% revenues): 7.2% pricing on CrunchMax chips/OatBliss cookies, trade spend down 150 bps to 22%, pocket margin +320 bps to 28.5%. Beverages: 5.8% on HydroSpark functional waters/low-sugar sodas. Dairy: 4.9%, but premium yogurts +9.1% ASPs.

Organic breakdown: price +4.3 points, volume +1.1 (vs. Kellogg's -2%), mix +2.8 from 'Elevate' premium (plant-based/zero-sugar) up 16% YoY to 28% revenues, like Nestlé/Danone.

Regions: North America (55%) 7.5% price, e-com 14%, EDLP. EMEA 4.2% price, +3% plant-based volume. APAC 8.9% price/+5% volume urban premium. LATAM 6.4%, 70% FX hedges.

Tech boosts: AI Dynamic Pricing Engine (NielsenIRI + loyalty app) at 92% accuracy, Zero-Base Trade reallocating $120M to shopper marketing (+11% repeats). 12 'FutureFit' SKUs with regen cocoa/functional, 2x velocity.

This yields profitable revenue, 50 bps annual margin gain. FY24 pricing 5.5-6.5%, Q4 Beverages focus. FY25 4-6% organic via 32% premium, blockchain traceability.

Now, capital expenditure plans and priorities for FY2024 and beyond. We're in a pivotal phase, with $1.6 billion full-year capex, up 12% from $1.43 billion in FY2023, signaling confidence amid easing inflation and stable sugar/dairy.

Allocation: 40% ($640M) capacity expansion, 30% ($480M) automation/digital, 20% ($320M) sustainability, 10% ($160M) maintenance. Targets ROIC >12%, 4-6% organic growth.

Capacity: debottlenecking plant-based snacks/RTD. North America (45% of $12 billion annual base): $250M Midwest aseptic plant for VitaShake, +20% capacity, H2 2025 production, <3-year payback like Danone Alpro. APAC (22% CAGR): $200M Vietnam low-sugar line for $15B RTD energy vs. Red Bull. LATAM: $120M Brazil snack upgrades for NutriCrunch, +15% throughput hedging 25% cocoa spike.

Automation/digital $480M: Industry 4.0 vs. labor inflation (200bps margin hit per McKinsey). $150M robotics/AI quality in 12 plants (Texas snacks: +25% throughput, -15% scrap like PepsiCo). $100M SAP S/4HANA/IoT for +10% utilization. EMEA $80M vision tech -30% rejects like Arla.

Sustainability $320M: 68% consumers prioritize eco (Kantar). $120M water recycling -25% usage vs. corn syrup droughts. $100M solar/boilers -18% Scope 1/2 by 2026 for green bonds like Unilever. $60M regen palm/coffee with Rainforest Alliance for $2B chain post-Ukraine.

Maintenance $160M: $50M cold chain for 15% e-com growth.

Prioritizes IRR >15%, <4-year paybacks; 60% ops-funded, 4.2% debt. FY2025 $1.5B as ramps, for buybacks/2.8% yield. Positions for premium health ($500B by 2027), snacks +12%.

Turning to organic sales growth guidance for Q4 and FY2025. Organic excludes M&A/FX/divestitures.

Q4: 4-6%, up from Q3 3.2%, modest volume + pricing.

Segments: Beverages (45%) 5-7% on AquaVita (+1.2 share, 85% club ACV), zero-sugar RTD coffee like KDP. Snacks/Convenience (35%) 3-5%, NutriCrunch +8% premium vs. Mondelez. Dairy/Plant (20%) flat-2%, GreenMoo stabilizing with aseptic Europe.

Regions: NA (55%) 5-7%, e-com 18% beverages, 2-3% pricing (2.1% CPI). EMEA (25%) 3-5%, functional snacks share +0.8 Lidl/Aldi, EcoPack -25% plastic. APAC/LATAM (20%) 2-4%, Brazil RTD tea 12% cat growth, China JV +6% noodles.

FY2025: 5-7%, high-end of 4-6% long-term. Assumes 2-3% CPI, no FX shocks.

Drivers: 2-3% volume via 50+ better-for-you SKUs. 2-4% pricing surgical. Channel to retail/e-com (+300bps margins), 15% SKU prune like Nestlé. SupplySync ERP 5% efficiency, ADM precision -8% fruit costs.

Risks: private label 28%, LatAm tariffs, value focus (62% consumers).

Embeds 'Growth Accelerator': innovate, price smart, margins 18-19%. Track record 5.4% past 3 years vs. PepsiCo 4%.

Finally, our full-year guidance, which we are reaffirming today with a slight upward tilt at the midpoint. Q3: $3.2 billion revenues +5% organic (3% volume/2% price), EBITDA margin +110bps to 24.2%, EPS $0.95 beat.

FY: adjusted EPS $3.50-$3.70, revenues narrowed/raised to $12.6-$13.0 billion (prior $12.4-$12.9B), 4-6% organic midpoint > initial 3-5%. Gross margins 45-46% (vs. 44% FY23), $250M productivity vs. FX/investments.

Drivers: premium/health tailwinds like Pepsi Gatorade/Core Hydration. PureVital +12% e-com/Walmart/Amazon. CSD volumes stabilize (Beverage Digest +1%).

Price/mix 3-4%, inflation eased (dairy -8%, PET -15%).

Regions: NA (65%) mid-single, hydration/plant snacks +4%/+18% Whole Foods/California/AFH. EMEA (20%) raised 5-7%, UK/Germany vs. Unilever Innocent. APAC/LATAM (15%) 6%, Brazil tea +10%, China improving localized.

Enablers: SAP Phase 2 80% plants, $80M savings (8.2x turns, +25% forecast Blue Yonder). $50M recycled PET for EU subsidies. ADM precision -10% pulp.

Optimization: divest snacks $150M for functional M&A like Mondelez Clif. R&D +15% to 2.5% sales, 20+ FY25 SKUs probiotics/zero-sugar ($50B functional per Euromonitor).

Risks: FX (10% Euro -2¢ EPS), El Niño commodities, rates/consumer. 45% FCF, $1.2B liquidity, 2.8x debt/EBITDA.

Conviction for mid-single growth, 25%+ ROIC.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for adjusted EPS $3.50 to $3.70 and revenues $12.6 to $13.0 billion.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thanks, John. Inflation remains a headwind, but we've navigated it effectively with 6.1% targeted pricing across the portfolio, directly offsetting 12-15% rises in cocoa, dairy, and oils. Our RGM framework, including AI-driven elasticity modeling and premium mix shifts, kept volumes resilient at +1.1 points while expanding pocket margins, particularly in Snacks. This positions us well as input costs stabilize.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Lisa Chen (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for ZestRevive and what is the expected impact of the product?

Taylor Kim (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Lisa. ZestRevive has exceeded expectations since Q1 launch, hitting $120 million in trailing sales with rapid 85% ACV in North America grocery and convenience. Plans include EMEA expansion via Tesco and further APAC rollouts, leveraging its zero-sugar adaptogen formula for the booming functional RTD space. We expect it to contribute 5-7 points to Beverages growth in FY25, with 48% gross margins and scaling e-com to 20% of volume, driving overall NPD to 20-25% of revenue uplift.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Mike Rodriguez (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Morgan Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Great question, Mike. We've prioritized resilience through our $1.6 billion capex, with 40% to capacity like the Midwest aseptic plant and Vietnam line to debottleneck high-demand categories. Automation investments—$480 million in robotics, AI quality control, and SAP IoT—have yielded 25% throughput gains and 15% scrap reductions, countering labor shortages. Sustainability plays like water recycling and regen ag partnerships hedge against droughts and cocoa volatility, while 70% FX hedges and cold chain upgrades support 15% e-com growth. These have minimized disruptions from weather and geopolitics, targeting 10% asset utilization uplift.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Emily White with Barclays. Please proceed.

Emily White (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Thanks, Emily. For Q4, we're guiding 4-6% organic sales growth, stepping up from Q3 on Beverages strength and regional momentum. Full-year reaffirms $12.6-13.0 billion revenues, 45-46% gross margins, and $3.50-3.70 EPS, with FY25 organic at 5-7%. This assumes stable macros, but our productivity, innovation pipeline, and strong balance sheet provide flexibility amid any consumer or commodity softness.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in VitaNutra Foods Inc. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
